sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A new camera system being tested on motorways in south-east England has detected thousands of illegal 'ghost plates' daily. These plates use reflective materials to make vehicle registrations unreadable to automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) cameras. Undercover filming by BBC Panorama revealed how easily and cheaply these plates can be purchased without legally required background checks.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Illegal plates allow drivers to avoid speed limits, low emission zones, and fines. Experts and police warn that these plates put the public at risk, help organised criminals evade tracking, and have been linked to fatal road crashes.

sections.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has announced the Your First Home scheme to assist first-time buyers in England. sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Swiss voters overwhelmingly rejected a proposal backed by the Swiss People's Party (SVP) to enshrine a stricter definition of armed neutrality into the constitution. Official results showed around 70% of voters, and all cantons, opposed the initiative. The measure would have barred Switzerland from joining military alliances or imposing sanctions without UN approval.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The vote allows Switzerland to continue cooperating with Nato and maintaining sanctions against Russia following its invasion of Ukraine. While the SVP and Russia supported the initiative, the federal government and most parties opposed it, arguing the changes would isolate Switzerland internationally and weaken security. The result confirms voters support the government's flexible interpretation of historic neutrality.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The Swiss People's Party accepted the referendum defeat and stated it has no current plans for further action.
